review_notes: I read the whole file. It defines tensorObj (an abbrev over the existing balanced tensor construction), tensorMap, a curried bifunctor tensorFunctor, and its Additive and Linear instances. I did not read the sibling files, and I did not search Mathlib for DG bimodule or balanced-tensor APIs. As far as I know, Mathlib has no DG-bimodule category or balanced tensor of DG bimodules, so there is nothing for these declarations to compete with. The generic constructions I know of are the monoidal tensor functor and `Functor.Additive` / `Functor.Linear`. The file uses the last two; it does not redefine them. tensorMap is a named wrapper that adds the equivariance and grading proofs on top of the existing `BalancedTensorProduct.map`, so it is not a competing duplicate. tensorFunctor is built from tensorObj and tensorMap, so it adds no second tensor concept. I found no justified finding. The remaining uncertainty is the sibling files, which I did not read.
